rationale:
ROUND 2 (resubmission after REVISE on 56e13695, gated by editquality). What changed: the two DETERMINISTIC match layers (path_key, canonical_name) shipped default-ON in round 1 on the argument that they ask the same question the exact-URL rename already asks unconditionally. The guardian and architecture seats both objected that this changes matching behaviour for every existing caller fleet-wide on deploy while the weaker stem layer got a dark launch, and that 'behaviour changed for an existing caller' is architecture-scope however sound the argument. ACCEPTED — the inconsistency was mine: I demanded measured evidence before enabling the layer I distrusted and exempted the two I preferred. All three layers are now gated (twin_identity_snap for the two deterministic ones, stem_twin_snap for the heuristic), all default OFF, and all COUNT what they would have done while off. The change is therefore now entirely opt-in/default-OFF with no live consumer, which is RFC_022's explicitly carved-out shape, so the needs_rfc trigger no longer applies.

THREE OBJECTIONS ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE RATHER THAN CODE. (1) editquality medium, the best objection of the round: does the identity_authority marker actually survive from the reconciler to the two write surfaces, given site_plan_pages has no column to carry it? It does, and not through that table — the live build-site-planner wires validate_plan's output_field to 'site_plan', and both surfaces read that key from collected_data via extractPagesFromPlan, which appends each page map WHOLE. Now PROVEN, not argued: TestReconcile_MarkerSurvivesTheStepBoundary drives the real extractor over a validate-shaped payload, and is mutation-checked (stop stamping the marker and it goes red). (2) prior_art_librarian high: resolveToolPageIdentity exists at deploy_tool_action.go:664 and does exactly what was cited — queries pages under both spellings, ORDER BY (name = canonical) DESC, keeps the stored identity. (3) editquality high + debug_historian medium, the three-pages-upsert-helpers landmine: only ONE of the two surfaces writes `pages` at all (SyncPagesToDBAction via upsertPage); WriteSitePlanAction writes site_plan_pages, the plan table. upsertPage is the correct helper by that landmine's own rule — a role arriving from a plan belongs on the plan-sync path, and UpsertPageForRole's ADOPT branch would hand a model-steered arm the authority bugs_closed/081 declined.

STILL OPEN AND RECORDED, not silently dropped. reuse_agent asks why the canonical layer does not extend check_page_canonical_collision: that check finds collisions in STORED state after the fact and deliberately mutates nothing (its header says visibility is the whole of its job), whereas this prevents them at plan time — a different moment on a different table, and the shared part (the two identity keys) IS extracted into datahelpers and used by both. PLAN-048 now states this. reuse_agent also asks about unifying with resolveToolPageIdentity: that helper answers 'which identity does this tool page already have' by querying the DB for one page in one arm; this answers 'which plan entries denote pages already realised' for a whole plan in memory. Unifying them would mean a per-page query inside the reconciler's loop. Stated rather than assumed.

----- ORIGINAL ROUND 1 RATIONALE FOLLOWS -----

bugs_open/215's REMAINING scope, the quiet mode. The crash mode (two plan entries canonicalising to one name, aborting the whole replan write) was fixed and proven live on v1.0.1276. The bug stayed OPEN, by the council's own round-1 ruling (corr 8ab18991, editquality objection 1: 'tracked, not dropped'), for the mode where a plan entry and an ALREADY-REALISED page carry two identities for one page. Nothing reconciles them, so SyncPagesToDBAction's upsert — which conflicts on (site_id, name) and nothing else, with no unique index on url — INSERTs a second pages row: status active, build_status planned, deployed_at NULL. That row is a permanent 404 and a valid internal-link target from creation.

WHY NOW, AND WHY IT IS WORSE THAN FILED. Measured 2026-08-11 on the live DB: SEVEN twin pairs across FOUR domains where BOTH spellings are deployed — i.e. duplicate live content, not merely phantom 404s (ai-agent-orchestration.com, finetuning.uk, fundamentallyai.com x2, robot-hands.com x3; all 14 URLs HTTP-tested, all 200, against a 404 control of 2697 bytes). And the same morning, TWO hand-archived phantom rows on fundamentallyai were rebuilt and re-deployed by the work-item pipeline (deployed_at stamped 10:34:21 and 11:13:25 today; both now serve 200), so the sweep front's hand-archive is not durable against the refile loop. That second finding is a DISTINCT defect about archived rows reaching the builder — filed separately to the 090 diagnosis loop (run correlation 38099787), not smuggled in here.

THE PART THAT CHANGES THE FILED PLAN, and the reason this is two coupled pieces rather than one. bugs_open/215 states the fix 'belongs in the reconciler'. That is correct about where the DECISION belongs and insufficient on its own, and I want the council to test this claim hardest: both canonicalisation surfaces re-derive every page's identity unconditionally (write_site_plan_action.go, site_db_actions.go), and CanonicalisePage CANNOT EXPRESS a legacy identity — a tool-typed page always comes back 'tool-<bare>' at the role's default hub. Measured: 71 live SHIPPED rows fleet-wide are not fixed points of the canonicaliser. For exactly that population a reconciler-only snap is silently undone downstream and the twin is re-minted by the very pass that spotted it. So the reconciler decides, and the writers must be told to stop overruling it.

WHAT IS OPT-IN AND WHY. Two site-level switches, both default FALSE (owner ruling 2026-08-02; RFC_022's 2026-08-11 interim puts this shape outside the architecture trigger). honour_realised_identity gates the writer half. stem_twin_snap gates the weakest matching layer, which is dark-launched: while OFF it still counts and durably records what it WOULD have done, so the decision to enable it rests on a measured population rather than an argument. Site-level rather than step config deliberately — a step config is a fleet-wide switch with no honest way to pilot it. The two default-ON layers (normalised path key, predicted canonical identity) are the SAME question Pass B already asks unconditionally, with comparators that can see the two ways the answer is yes; the canonical layer merely front-runs a collapse the write path performs one step later anyway.

plan.summary: Close bugs_open/215's quiet mode: layered twin-identity matching in reconcilePlanWithRealised (two layers default ON, one opt-in and dark-launched), plus an opt-in guard so both canonicalisation surfaces honour a realised identity instead of re-deriving it. Shared identity keys extracted to datahelpers per the IMG-070 third-instance rule. Every snap and every refusal is a durable agent_error_log row.

edits.rationale: The three identity keys already existed, hand-copied into whichever package needed them (pageURLPathKey and collisionCanonName in discovery_checks; itemStemOf in v3_site_actions.go, carrying the comment 'keep this prefix list in sync with them' as its only guard). This fix needs all three in a THIRD place, which is precisely the trigger IMG-070's round-3 reuse note names: the third instance builds the shared datahelpers utility rather than another copy. They live beside CanonicalisePage because every one is derived from a rule CanonicalisePage itself applies, and a copy that drifts from it is silently wrong rather than loudly broken. The original call sites now delegate, so behaviour is unchanged and their existing tests keep pinning it at the point of use. COMMITTED 65c1984d0.

ONE fact, ONE reader — the rule site_url_shape.go states for the flat-URL flag and for the same reason: these two surfaces diverging over a rule one applies and the other does not is a previously-shipped regression (PLAN-003). If they disagree about who owns an identity, the plan and the pages table carry different names for one page, which is WORSE than the bug being fixed because it breaks the site_plan_pages.name = pages.name join that check_sectionless_pages and reconcile_site_plan both depend on. Site-level rather than step config so the switch can be piloted where the population has actually been measured. realisedIdentityOf fails safe in both directions: only the exact marker value counts, and a marked page missing any identity field falls through to canonicalisation rather than writing a blank. COMMITTED 65c1984d0.

GATED IN ROUND 2. The reconciler matched realised pages only by exact URL (Pass B) and exact name (Pass B2); Pass C2's stem dedup is structurally first-plan-only, so on every re-plan nothing looks for twins at all. Three new keys, strongest first, all refusing a key two realised pages claim (the buildCanonicalPageNameMap convention: when two pages want one alias, guessing is worse than missing). Pass B's snap body is EXTRACTED rather than copied, so all four match routes apply identical section rules — the bugs_open/050 empty-page routing and the fact-assignment carry the 151 lane measures. Snap, never drop: dropping is what Pass C2 does and it discards the plan-time fact assignments with the entry, which Pass A's union cannot carry back. The stem layer needs EXACTLY ONE side prefixed, which makes the on-record false positive (tool-pricing beside guide-pricing) structurally unmatchable rather than merely unlikely, and it runs in BOTH directions because the direction flips in real data — a defect this fixture set caught during implementation, when the layer was silently inert on the very shape that cost fundamentallyai a phantom. ROUND 2 CHANGE: path_key and canonical_name are no longer default-ON. Both now sit behind the site-level twin_identity_snap (default OFF) and, while off, record PLAN_PAGE_IDENTITY_TWIN_OBSERVED rows and increment TwinIdentityObserved — the same dark-launch discipline the stem layer already had. Pinned by TestReconcile_DeterministicLayersAreGatedAndCountWhenOff, mutation-checked by forcing the gate true.

edits.rationale: Stamps identity_authority=realised and carries parent_section. Placed HERE rather than in the snap helper so Pass A's UNION is covered too, not only snaps: a preserved realised page the planner omitted is re-added and then re-canonicalised at the write path, which can rename or move it — the same exposure by a different route. parent_section is recovered from the realised URL's directory and matters even while the flag is off: without it CanonicalisePage re-derives a blog-post's URL under /blog/, which MOVES a page serving from /guides/ (bugs_open/241's damage shape, measured on fundamentallyai's guide twins). The reconciler is the only minter — it deletes any marker present on LLM input before any pass reads it, so a plan cannot forge one. DURABLE RECORDS, same edit: three codes on agent_error_log (PLAN_PAGE_IDENTITY_SNAPPED, PLAN_PAGE_STEM_TWIN_OBSERVED, PLAN_PAGE_STEM_TWIN_REFUSED) plus five named reconcileCounts fields. Durable and not log-only because an active chassis pod retains under one second of log (bugs_open/136 section 11) — the finding that conditioned the 08-10 richer-wins ruling. OBSERVED is the dark-launch measurement (each row is also a phantom about to be minted); REFUSED exists because a silent guard is indistinguishable from a dead one.

edits.rationale: THE EDIT MOST WORTH ATTACKING, and the one the filed bug does not call for. Without it the reconciler's decision does not survive: both surfaces re-run CanonicalisePage over every page, and for the 71 measured live rows whose stored identity is not a fixed point of the canonicaliser the twin is re-minted regardless of what the plan decided. Gated on the site policy, unsafe default OFF, read through the ONE shared helper so the two surfaces cannot diverge. The estate already has this exact authority at another surface: resolveToolPageIdentity (deploy_tool_action.go) queries pages under BOTH spellings and its header states an existing row 'keeps its stored identity untouched'. Mutation-proved: removing the guard from either file leaves every unit test green and fails only the wiring test, which is why that test exists.

The SECOND of the two surfaces, and the one where the phantom is actually INSERTed: upsertPage conflicts on (site_id, name) and nothing else, so a re-derivation here mints the twin no matter what the plan says. It must carry the identical guard, read from the identical helper — these two diverging over a rule one applies and the other does not is a previously-shipped regression (PLAN-003), and divergence here is WORSE than the bug being fixed because it breaks the site_plan_pages.name = pages.name join. Mutation-proved: neutering this one surface leaves every unit test green and fails only TestIdentityPolicyReachesBothCanonicalisationSurfaces.

One line. A snap replaces the planner's spelling, so an imagery block keyed to it would fall to the miss path and be written verbatim as an orphan — true of today's Pass B snaps already, and this change widens that window, so it is fixed rather than inherited. planPageRow gains ReconciledFrom (written to no column, like RawName). The existing ambiguity machinery still refuses a spelling two pages claim. This IMPROVES bugs_open/214's name-space mismatch rather than worsening it.

Every fixture is a shape MEASURED on the live fleet on 2026-08-11, not invented to suit the code — the fix's whole claim is that these pairs occur, so invented fixtures would prove the code self-consistent and nothing else. Premise-pinning follows TestCanonicalisePage_CollapseFamilies: if PageItemStem stops inverting the canonicaliser's prefixes, the suite says so rather than leaving the key quietly blind to a family. False-positive fixtures are first-class: tool-pricing/guide-pricing must NOT match, a multi-claimant stem is refused, and a both-deployed pair in the plan is refused. Mutation evidence recorded: pass-through fails 5 tests; deleting the path-key layer fails its own test (and reveals the canonical layer catching the same fixture, which the assertion on WHICH layer fired detects); removing the exactly-one-prefix guard fails the false-positive test; dropping the both-in-plan refusal fails the robot-hands test; not stripping the forged marker fails its test; removing the writer guard from one surface leaves all unit tests green and fails only the wiring test.

grounded_in: MEASURED 2026-08-11, current plans joined to realised pages with differing names: normalised-path key matches 3 pairs, stem key matches 11, and a human read ZERO of them as genuinely different pages. The population is confined to fundamentallyai.com and robot-hands.com.

MEASURED 2026-08-11: 7 twin pairs across 4 domains where BOTH spellings are deployed. All 14 URLs HTTP-tested and serving 200; the 404 control returns 2697 bytes, so the 200s are content and not the error page. Component counts differ per side (robot-hands: 5/3/4 against 1 each), so the two sides are different builds — which is why remediation is an owner call per pair and NOT automated here.

MEASURED 2026-08-11: 71 live SHIPPED rows fleet-wide whose stored identity is not a fixed point of CanonicalisePage. This is the population for which a reconciler-only fix is inert, and the whole justification for the writer guard.

page_canonical.go, role 'tool': `return "tool-" + bare, nestedOrFlatURL(dir, bare, d.FlatURLs), "tool"` — the canonicaliser cannot emit a legacy identity, so honouring one cannot be expressed as a canonicalisation option.

site_db_actions.go upsertPage: `INSERT INTO pages (...) ON CONFLICT (site_id, name) DO UPDATE SET url = EXCLUDED.url` — name-only conflict, and `pages` has no unique index on url (confirmed in bugs_open/215 correction 1 and in check_page_canonical_collision.go's own header), so a differing name INSERTs rather than conflicts.

v3_site_actions.go Pass C2 header: 'Deliberately still scoped to the FIRST-PLAN subset ... a false positive suppresses a legitimately new page (a new "tool-pricing" beside a built "guide-pricing" shares the stem "pricing")' — the stated risk this change answers structurally rather than by argument.

Council verdict corr 8ab18991, editquality objection 1: 'dedupePlanPageRows only dedupes within one planRows batch — it cannot see rows already persisted from a prior plan or the live pages table, so the cited quiet-mode mechanism is untouched.' Disposition: tracked, owner named as the reconciler against realised pages under either spelling.

Owner ruling 2026-08-11 section 1: 'The phantom-mode fix stays in bugs_open/215's remaining scope on its own merits' — this work is in scope and is not competing with the fact-assignment lane's authorised census replan.
IMG-070 register entry: 'A THIRD instance should trigger the shared datahelpers utility, not another copy — the reuse seat's round-3 note says exactly this.'
plan.risks:
WHAT I AM ASKING THE COUNCIL TO ATTACK HARDEST: the writer guard is authority the filed bug did not ask for, and its necessity rests on one measurement (71 non-fixed-point rows). If that measurement is wrong the guard is unnecessary complexity at the estate's most-shared write path. It is opt-in and default OFF, so it changes nothing until a site opts in — but it is still the edit to distrust.

DELIBERATELY NOT ADDRESSED. (1) The 7 both-deployed pairs: content differs per side, survivor choice trades SEO against convention, and robot-hands has no loop-safe archive order until a replan lands. Owner call per pair, delivered as a runbook, not automated Go. (2) Archived pages being rebuilt and re-deployed by the work-item pipeline — measured live today, a DISTINCT defect, filed to the 090 loop (corr 38099787) rather than smuggled in here. (3) reconcile_site_plan's loadRealisedPages has no status filter; named because it is adjacent and is part of that separate defect, not changed here.

KNOWN INTERACTIONS. bugs_open/204: pages.sections on five decomposed sites holds positional slot names, and normaliseRealisedToPlanPage carries them verbatim — the fact-carry miss path handles this durably, but a snapped decomposed page whose slots later fail component resolution is a hazard I have NOT closed; those five sites should not have the flags enabled until 204 is fixed. bugs_open/151: the fact-assignment measurement flows through the arm I extracted; behaviour is pinned by the existing tests plus a new one, and the extraction is refactor-only for the exact-URL route.

SEAM CONSUMERS TOLD, not merely measured (2026-07-29 ruling): the build-site-planner pipeline (both write surfaces), the fact-assignment front (Pass B/B2 carry semantics unchanged), imagery scope resolution (improved), check_sectionless_pages (its join matches MORE after a snap, not less), and reconcile_site_plan (its needs_page stream stops naming twins once plan names converge). What changed about their guarantee: a plan page derived from a realised page now keeps that page's stored identity, where before it was re-derived.
